title: Things to Do in Warangal: Kakatiya Gateways, Ramappa Temple & Forest Lakes
seoTitle: Things to Do in Warangal: Ramappa & Kakatiya Sites | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Warangal: the Warangal Fort and Kakatiya Kala Thoranam gateways, the Thousand Pillar Temple, the UNESCO-listed Ramappa Temple, Bhadrakali Temple and lake, Laknavaram's hanging bridge, Bogatha waterfall, Pakhal Lake and the Medaram Jatara.
dek: The old capital of the Kakatiya dynasty in Telangana, known for its carved stone gateways, star-shaped temples and a UNESCO-listed masterpiece in the countryside.
searchIntent: Heritage travellers and weekenders from Hyderabad planning one or two days in Warangal.

hero.caption: Ramappa Temple

intro: Warangal, about 150 km north-east of Hyderabad, was the capital of the Kakatiya dynasty from the 12th to the early 14th century. The Kakatiyas built reservoirs, forts and temples in a distinctive style, with star-shaped plans, black basalt pillars and intricate carvings. Their gateway arch, the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam, is the emblem of Telangana.

The things to do in Warangal include the ruins of Warangal Fort, the Thousand Pillar Temple in Hanamkonda, the Bhadrakali Temple on its lake, and a trip to the Ramappa Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2021. The forests and lakes of Mulugu district, such as Laknavaram and Bogatha waterfall, add nature to the trip.
One to two days is enough. October to February is the most comfortable time.
quickAnswer: See the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam at Warangal Fort
Walk the hanging bridge at Laknavaram Lake

items.name: See Warangal Fort

image.alt: Kakatiya Kala Thoranam gateway at Warangal Fort
image.caption: Kakatiya Kala Thoranam

body: Warangal Fort, begun in the 13th century, once had concentric walls of earth and stone. Inside, the ruins of a great Shiva temple are marked by four magnificent carved stone gateways, the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam, and scattered sculptures. A sound and light show is held in the evening.

items.name: Visit the Thousand Pillar Temple
body: The Thousand Pillar Temple in Hanamkonda, built in 1163 under King Rudra Deva, is a star-shaped temple dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu and Surya, with finely carved pillars and a large Nandi carved from a single stone.
The temple has three shrines arranged around a central hall, and the Nandi in front is polished black basalt. Restoration work has reassembled parts of the mandapa.

items.name: See the Ramappa Temple
body: The Ramappa (Rudreswara) Temple at Palampet, about 70 km away, was built in 1213 and is named after its sculptor. Its bracket figures of dancers and mythical beasts, carved in polished black basalt, are among the finest in India. The temple is famous for its roof bricks, which are light enough to float. It was listed by UNESCO in 2021.

The temple stands near the Ramappa lake, another Kakatiya reservoir, and a small Kameshwara temple and other shrines lie in the same complex. Local guides explain the dancer figures, which are said to reflect the Perini Shivatandavam dance form.

items.name: See the Kush Mahal
body: The Kush Mahal, a later royal hall near the fort built in the 14th century, has a small collection of sculptures.

items.name: Visit Bhadrakali Temple

image.alt: Bhadrakali Temple on its lake, Warangal
image.caption: Bhadrakali Temple

body: The Bhadrakali Temple, on a hill between Warangal and Hanamkonda, is dedicated to the goddess Kali. It overlooks the Bhadrakali lake and is especially busy during Navratri.

items.name: Walk the hanging bridge at Laknavaram
body: Laknavaram Lake, a Kakatiya-era reservoir about 70 km away in forested hills, has suspension bridges linking small islands, boating and lakeside cottages. It is especially beautiful after the monsoon.

items.name: See Bogatha waterfall
body: Bogatha waterfall, deep in the forests of Mulugu district, is a wide cascade often called the Niagara of Telangana. It is at its best in and after the monsoon; swimming in the pool is restricted in high flow.

items.name: Relax at Pakhal Lake
body: Pakhal Lake, another Kakatiya reservoir from the 13th century, lies inside a wildlife sanctuary and is a quiet place for birdwatching.

items.name: Buy Warangal durries
body: Warangal durries, flat-woven cotton rugs with a GI tag, are made by weavers in Kothawada. Workshops and shops sell them in many colours and patterns.

items.name: Attend the Medaram Jatara
body: The Sammakka Saralamma Jatara at Medaram, held every two years in February, is one of the largest tribal festivals in the world, honouring two Koya women warriors. Millions attend, offering jaggery as bangaram (gold).

items.name: Eat Telangana food
body: Try Telangana dishes such as sarva pindi (a spicy rice-flour pancake), jonna rotte (sorghum flatbread) and spicy chicken and mutton curries.

items.name: October to February
body: Pleasant weather for temples and forts, and lakes full after the monsoon.

items.name: March to June
body: Very hot; visit monuments early in the morning or late in the afternoon.

items.name: July to September
body: The monsoon fills the lakes and waterfalls and turns the forests green, a good time for Bogatha and Laknavaram.

byTraveller.text: The fort, the Thousand Pillar Temple and a half day at Ramappa.
Laknavaram's bridges and boating, Bhadrakali Temple and the fort's light show.
Drive out on Saturday for Warangal's monuments and spend Sunday at Ramappa and Laknavaram.

oneDay: Visit the Thousand Pillar Temple and Bhadrakali Temple in the morning, then drive to Palampet for the Ramappa Temple. Stop at Laknavaram Lake on the way back, and end at Warangal Fort for the evening light and sound show.
tips: Warangal and Kazipet have railway stations; Hyderabad airport is about three hours away.
Ramappa and Laknavaram are best combined in one day.
Carry water and a hat; there is little shade at the fort.
Start early for Ramappa and Laknavaram; the forest roads are slow.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Warangal?
faqs.a: See Warangal Fort and the Kakatiya gateways, the Thousand Pillar Temple, the Ramappa Temple and Bhadrakali Temple, walk the bridges at Laknavaram and see Bogatha waterfall.

faqs.q: How far is Ramappa Temple from Warangal?
faqs.a: About 70 km, roughly one and a half hours by road.

faqs.q: Is Ramappa Temple a UNESCO site?
faqs.a: Yes. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Warangal?
What is the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam?
faqs.a: It is the carved stone gateway at Warangal Fort built by the Kakatiya dynasty, now the emblem of Telangana.
